chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sadan ibn Muslim, from Mu'alla ibn Khunays, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) went out on a night when it had sprinkled (rain), intending the shelter of Banu Sa'idah. I followed him, and something fell from him, so he said, 'In the name of Allah, O Allah, return it to us.' I approached him, greeted him, and he said, 'Mu'alla.' I said, 'Yes, may I be your ransom.' He said to me, 'Look for what you have, and whatever you find of something, deliver it to me.' So I found a lot of scattered bread, and I began delivering to him whatever I found. Then I found a bag heavy with bread that I could hardly carry, so I said, 'May I be your ransom, I will carry it on my shoulder.' He said, 'No, I am more deserving of it than you, but proceed with me.' We arrived at the shelter of Banu Sa'idah, and we found a group of people sleeping. He began distributing one loaf and two loaves until he reached the last of them. Then we returned. I said, 'May I be your ransom, do these people know the truth?' He said, 'If they knew it, we would comfort them with the salt.' And the salt is the milh.

Indeed, Allah did not create anything except that He has a guardian to store it, except for charity, for the Lord manages it Himself. And my father, whenever he gave charity, would place it in the hand of the beggar, then take it back from him, kiss it, smell it, and then return it to the hand of the beggar.
Indeed, the charity of the night extinguishes the anger of the Lord, Exalted, erases the great sin, and lightens the reckoning. And the charity of the day yields wealth and increases longevity.

Indeed, Jesus, son of Mary (peace be upon him), when he passed by the shore of the sea, threw a piece of his food into the water. Some of the disciples said, 'O Spirit of Allah and His Word, why did you do this? It is only a piece of your food.' He said, 'I did this for a beast that eats it from the beasts of the water, and its reward with Allah is great.'
ai.seo_question: What are the specific spiritual and worldly benefits of giving charity at night versus during the day according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on obligatory alms (*Zakat*) to the Imam, this hadith illustrates the practical application of charitable distribution by Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) to the community. It distinguishes between the spiritual purification of night charity, which extinguishes divine anger, and the material blessings of day charity, while emphasizing the etiquette of dignified giving through the example of his father, Imam al-Baqir. The narrative further connects human charity to divine care, citing Jesus (peace be upon him) feeding aquatic creatures to demonstrate that even small acts yield immense reward.
